problem: Existing VLN agents (e.g. DUET) explore blindly because they lack explicit spatial proximity knowledge. Prior knowledge-based methods (ConceptNet, Visual Genome) use non-navigation-specific knowledge and only consider proximity between the current node and the target, ignoring intermediate transit nodes.
motivation: Navigating to a target requires common-sense reasoning about which room types lead to which (e.g. a bathroom is near a bedroom, not a recreation room). The paper extracts node/object adjacency statistics directly from the navigation environments and uses them for multi-step planning over the topological map, instead of relying on external knowledge bases.
key_idea: Build a hierarchical spatial proximity knowledge base (node-node, object-object, node-object) via a scene understanding auxiliary task, then use it for multi-step top-K path reasoning that yields sub-goal proximity scores fused residually with DUET's visual scores.
insight: Proximity knowledge mined from the environment itself is more useful than ConceptNet knowledge (REVERIE val-unseen SR 52.94 vs 50.10 vs base 46.98). The ConceptNet probabilities are concentrated in a narrow 0.4-0.55 range and give weak cues. Multi-step reasoning peaks at 3 steps (SPL 38.05) and degrades beyond that because deeper inferred nodes become unreliable. Residual fusion beats average and dynamic fusion (SR 52.94 vs 50.87 and 52.07).
method: Scene understanding auxiliary task: counts node-type adjacency (from segmented regions), object co-occurrence, and node-object correlation matrices; clips outliers at the 95th percentile and min-max normalizes each row to a proximity probability matrix in [0, 0.95]
Node recognition: self-attention over view and object features plus an FC layer predicts the type of each navigable node, trained with cross-entropy loss L_R

Proximity calculating: a target-aware attention layer predicts the target node type and object type from the instruction; node proximity score = node-type probability times the proximity matrix times the target-type probability; object proximity is computed likewise

Multi-step reasoning navigation: keeps the top-K highest-confidence paths over node types, treats the next intermediate node as a sub-goal, and falls back to a sub-optimal path; scores are discount-weighted over m steps (gamma=0.9, best m=3)

Residual fusion: adds proximity scores to DUET's global and local visual scores, and assigns non-local navigable nodes the global score (proximity + visual) instead of dynamic fusion's summed visited-node scores; a balancing factor beta_t combines local and global scores

Training: built on DUET (pre-training with MLM, MRC, SAP, OG; fine-tuning with a pseudo interactive demonstrator); total loss 0.2 L_SAP + L_PID + L_OG + L_R; Floyd algorithm for path planning on the map at inference

setting.backbone: DUET dual-scale graph transformer with proximity reasoning modules (LXMERT-initialized text encoder, ViT-B/16 features; trained)
setting.training_data: Benchmark training sets (REVERIE, SOON, R2R, R4R) with DUET-style pre-training (MLM, MRC, SAP, OG) plus the auxiliary node recognition task; proximity knowledge built from the training environments' segmentation and object labels
setting.observation: Panoramic RGB (36 views) with object features, discrete topological map
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (navigable nodes plus stop)
setting.privileged: Scene semantic segmentation and object labels of training scenes used to build the proximity knowledge base and node type labels; none stated at test time

numbers_note: The method is named HSPR in the text but labeled STPR in the tables. The R2R table does not report OSR.
results: HSPR beats the strongest baseline (KERM/DUET) on REVERIE val-unseen by +2.50 SR and +2.67 SPL (SR 52.94, SPL 38.05). On SOON test it reaches SR 39.3 and SPL 27.3 against the reproduced DUET's 33.4 and 21.4. It also gains on R2R (val-unseen SR 73.27) and R4R (val-unseen SR 46.94, SPL 43.96), with smaller gains on R2R than on REVERIE.
limitations: Gains on R2R are modest (test-unseen SPL +0.09 over KERM), since the method is aimed at coarse-grained goal-oriented navigation
Multi-step reasoning degrades beyond 3 steps because inferred intermediate nodes become unreliable
Only evaluated in discrete simulated environments and needs region segmentation labels to build the knowledge base; continuous environments are left as future work
